user_prompt: What is the effect of extended-duration anticoagulation, compared with standard-duration anticoagulation, on major bleeding within 45 days (short-term) in acutely ill medical patients receiving venous thromboembolism prophylaxis? This is the single target outcome: major bleeding, short-term (45 days or fewer), from the PRIMARY analysis only. Do NOT include the COVID-19-only sensitivity analysis, the same-extended-agent sensitivity analysis, or any subgroup analysis (by sex, age, cancer history, D-dimer status, or infection status) — these are separate, related analyses in this review using the same outcome label. Do NOT include symptomatic VTE, all-cause mortality, or any long-term (more than 45 days) outcome. This is dichotomous (event/no-event) data — please pool it as a Risk Ratio (RR), using each trial's reported number of major bleeding events and total randomized per arm. Note: extended-duration anticoagulation is the treatment/intervention arm, but for this particular outcome a HIGHER event rate is the worse (harmful) result for it — major bleeding is a safety/harm outcome, not a benefit outcome, so do not assume the treatment arm having more events is an extraction error. Note: if a trial reports zero major bleeding events in BOTH arms, that is expected for at least two of the trials in this review and should be treated as "not estimable" for this ratio measure, excluded from pooling rather than continuity-corrected.
